minutes.headline: TriBoard split near evenly on one FY27 override vs. two tiers, but agreed unanimously to put one on the ballot.
minutes.summary: The Select Board, Finance Committee and School Committee met jointly to debate how to structure a Proposition 2½ override for next year's budget, weighing a single combined ask against tiered options. Every member present favored putting some override on the ballot, but the group was closely divided over one number versus two, and no final figure was set that night. Town Counsel joined by phone to explain ballot procedure and campaign-finance limits, and the boards deferred a joint public statement, aiming to settle on a number in the coming weeks.

what_happened.line: The three boards voted unanimously to place a Proposition 2½ override question on the ballot, with no final amount set that night.
A straw poll on a single combined override versus two tiered options came out closely split, with the count itself unclear in the recording and several members absent.
Rather than issue a joint statement on the straw poll, each board agreed to share updates through its own channels, since the Select Board had not yet finished its own line-by-line budget review.
The boards set a goal of agreeing on an override number by late March or early April, ahead of the deadline to hand ballot language to the town clerk.
The School Committee will present its balanced, cuts-based budget at its March 18 meeting.

why_it_matters: Whatever number the boards settle on becomes the property tax increase every household is asked to approve at town meeting.

A single override versus a tiered one changes what is guaranteed to residents versus what depends on a second vote later — school staff positions were named specifically as at stake in either version.
The March 18 School Committee presentation of the cuts budget is the baseline every override option is being measured against.
watch_next: School Committee meeting, March 18, 2026 — presentation of the balanced/cuts budget
A tri-board decision on override structure and amount, targeted for late March/early April 2026, ahead of the ballot-language deadline

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: Once the caption-mangled names and figures are resolved, the two records agree closely on substance: the sequence of speakers, the two straw polls, the timeline pressure (March 18 cuts budget, end-of-March/early-April target, April 11 clerk deadline), and most dollar figures. The two things a reader should check are (1) our minutes record a vote nominating a member to a joint override-messaging subcommittee that the official minutes never mention at all, and (2) our minutes attach a $3M/$636 household-impact figure to the public-comment section at t=8492 when the official minutes show that exact figure was given earlier by the Town Manager, not by a public commenter.
